title: arrayfun
summary: Apply a function element-wise across array inputs in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Executes directly on the GPU for supported floating builtin callbacks when all inputs are gpuArray values; otherwise gathers exact typed storage, evaluates on the host, and re-uploads uniform numeric or logical output. All eight resident integer classes retain exact input and output storage through fallback.

description: `arrayfun(func, A1, A2, ...)` evaluates a scalar callback for each element or element-wise tuple. Ordinary host inputs must have the same size; the documented gpuArray overload accepts compatible sizes. `UniformOutput` controls array-versus-cell collection, and `ErrorHandler` receives the documented identifier, message, and linear index when a callback fails.
behaviors: The documented callable form is a function handle. Character-vector and string-scalar callable names are a mode-gated RunMat extension.
Host arrays require equal sizes. Host scalar expansion is a mode-gated RunMat extension; gpuArray input follows the documented compatible-size expansion rule.

`UniformOutput` accepts logical true/false or double 1/0. Typed-integer controls reject. With uniform output, every callback or error-handler result must be scalar and retain one data type; all eight integer classes, native single, and complex single are collected without widening.

Host `UniformOutput` and `ErrorHandler` implement the documented single-output control flow. With gpuArray input these options are a mode-gated RunMat extension because the GPU overload exposes scalar uniform outputs only.

The current implementation handles numeric, logical, character, string, and complex arrays. Standard multiple-output callbacks and cell, struct, and user-object inputs remain general callback/container gaps.
Empty inputs return empty outputs whose shape matches the first array argument.

When any input is a gpuArray, supported builtin callbacks may dispatch directly; otherwise authoritative typed inputs gather for callback evaluation and numeric or logical uniform outputs are uploaded back to the provider. Complex or character uniform outputs remain on the host.

examples.description: Squaring every element of a matrix

examples.input:
strings = ["Run" "Matlab" "GPU"];
chars = arrayfun(@(s) sprintf("%d", strlength(s)), strings, 'UniformOutput', false)

examples.description: Handling errors with a custom error handler

faqs.question: Do I have to call `gpuArray` before using `arrayfun`?
faqs.answer: No. `arrayfun` participates in the same planner as other builtins, so the runtime migrates data to the GPU when it determines a benefit. Manual `gpuArray` calls remain useful for MATLAB compatibility or to force residency for custom workflows.

faqs.question: What happens when the callback returns mixed types?
faqs.answer: Set `'UniformOutput', false` so the builtin returns a cell array. When `'UniformOutput'` is true, every callback invocation must return a scalar of the same data type; RunMat rejects heterogeneous results instead of promoting them.

faqs.question: Can `arrayfun` handle character inputs?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each character element is passed to the callback as a single-character char array and the output follows the normal uniform/non-uniform rules.

faqs.question: Does `arrayfun` short-circuit on errors?
faqs.answer: No. The builtin invokes the optional error handler when a callback fails. If no handler is provided the first error aborts the entire call with a MATLAB-compatible identifier/message pair.

faqs.question: How are logical outputs represented on the GPU?
faqs.answer: Logical results use 0.0/1.0 buffers on the device. When you gather them RunMat converts the data back into a logical array automatically.

gpu_residency: No. RunMat's auto-offload logic moves tensors to the GPU when profitable. If you do call `gpuArray`, `arrayfun` keeps the result on the GPU for uniform numeric or logical outputs so later operations can continue without gathering. Non-uniform or complex/character results stay on the host until GPU representations are available.
gpu_behavior: When every input is a gpuArray, uniform output is implicit, and the callback resolves to one of the supported builtins (`sin`, `cos`, `abs`, `exp`, `log`, `sqrt`, `plus`, `minus`, `times`, `rdivide`, or `ldivide`), RunMat can dispatch directly through provider hooks. The builtin remains a fusion barrier because arbitrary callback code may execute. Other documented GPU forms use compatible-size typed gather fallback and re-upload uniform numeric or logical results, including exact integer classes. GPU options, host scalar expansion, and text callables are separately mode-gated RunMat extensions; complex, character, and cell outputs remain host-resident.
